kept.row: Project servers in `<project>/.mcp.json`, approved by `enabledMcpjsonServers` and `enableAllProjectMcpServers` and rejected by `disabledMcpjsonServers`, settings keys of any settings file; a rejection in any file wins; a folder not trusted takes approval only from `~/.claude/settings.json`. Trust is `hasTrustDialogAccepted` under `projects.<path>` in `~/.claude.json`, of the folder or, in a git repository, a folder above it up to the root. Earlier versions kept the three keys there under `projects.<path>`; 2.1.311 moves them to `.claude/settings.local.json` the next time it starts in the folder, so Kitden reads both (2026-11-15, version 2.1.311, macOS)
kept.title: Plugin MCP servers use project approval
kept.changed: MCP servers declared by a project-scope plugin go through the same per-server approval as a project .mcp.json, and the trust check applies.
kept.user_gets: The user sees plugin MCP servers as on that the client has not approved, rejected or would not load in an untrusted folder, so they believe those servers are running.
kept.why: _plugin_parts() gives a plugin's MCP servers the plugin's enabled state and never runs _approval() or is_trusted() on them. The note says project-scope plugin servers now need per-server approval, but it does not say whether this covers user-scope plugins or how plugin servers are named in the approval keys, so how far the mismatch goes is a guess.
kept.fix: In src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py, for plugins enabled at project scope, apply _approval() and is_trusted() to the MCP servers that _plugin_parts() reads. Confirm the approval key names for plugin servers first.

kept.title: Managed MCP config managed-mcp.json
kept.changed: The release names `managed-mcp.json`, an administrator-provided file that affects which MCP servers load.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show the servers from managed-mcp.json or that they stop other MCP servers from loading.
kept.why: No row names managed-mcp.json or covers administrator-managed MCP servers.
kept.fix: Read the managed-mcp.json file in the system managed settings location and show its servers and its effect on other servers.

kept.piece: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading#Enabled in project settings but not installed
kept.title: Plugin seed directory
kept.changed: Plugins in a seed directory load with no install.
kept.user_gets: Plugins loaded from a seed directory are not shown.
kept.why: No row names a seed directory; plugin rows cover only installed_plugins.json and settings.
kept.fix: Read the seed directory location and list the plugins in it.

kept.title: CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR relocates plugins root
kept.changed: An environment variable moves the folder where plugins, caches and install records are kept.
kept.user_gets: If the variable is set, plugins installed under the relocated root are not shown.
kept.why: No row covers an environment variable that decides where plugins load from; CC-14 names only the fixed default path.
kept.fix: Read CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR and use it as the plugins root when finding installed_plugins.json and known_marketplaces.json.

kept.title: Managed settings enable or block plugins
kept.changed: Managed settings can force-enable or block plugins via enabledPlugins, overriding every other source.
kept.user_gets: Kitden shows plugins as on or off per user, project and local files, missing plugins forced on or blocked by managed policy.
kept.why: No row names managed settings as a source of enabledPlugins.
kept.fix: Kitden would need to read the managed settings file or policy location for enabledPlugins.

kept.title: disableAllHooks setting turns off hooks
kept.changed: A settings key `disableAllHooks` stops all hooks from running, resolved by settings precedence; managed settings hooks still run unless set there.
kept.user_gets: Kitden lists hooks as active even when disableAllHooks switches them off.
kept.why: CC-22 only says hooks live in the hooks key of settings files; no row covers a setting that decides whether hooks load.
kept.fix: Read `disableAllHooks` from the user, project, local and managed settings files and apply precedence.

kept.title: Plugin hooks/hooks.json as hook source
kept.changed: Hooks can come from a plugin's hooks/hooks.json file, active when the plugin is enabled.
kept.user_gets: Hooks bundled with enabled plugins are not shown.
kept.why: CC-22 covers only the hooks key of settings files, not plugin hook files.
kept.fix: Read hooks/hooks.json in each enabled plugin's install folder.

kept.title: Per-project disabledMcpServers list
kept.changed: A project-level disabledMcpServers list turns off MCP servers for that project.
kept.user_gets: Kitden shows a server as active that Claude Code has disabled for the project.
kept.why: No row names disabledMcpServers; CC-04 covers only the .mcp.json approval keys.
kept.fix: Read the disabledMcpServers list for each project and mark the servers it names as off.

kept.title: Enterprise managed skills location
kept.changed: Skills are loaded from a `.claude/skills` folder inside the managed settings directory for all users on a machine.
kept.user_gets: Skills deployed by the organization in the managed settings directory are not shown.
kept.why: No row covers the managed settings directory as a skill source; CC-20 names only the home and project skills folders.
kept.fix: Read the `.claude/skills` folder inside the managed settings directory.

kept.title: Skill folders with plugin.json load as skills-dir plugins
kept.changed: A skill folder in ~/.claude/skills or <project>/.claude/skills containing .claude-plugin/plugin.json is loaded as a plugin named <name>@⁠skills-dir, bringing its own agents, hooks and MCP servers.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show the agents, hooks and MCP servers that come from skills-dir plugins, nor that the skill folder is a plugin.
kept.why: Rows cover skill folders with SKILL.md, installed_plugins.json and the @⁠skills-dir id only as having no install; none reads plugin.json inside skill folders or the MCP servers, hooks and agents it bundles.
kept.fix: Read .claude-plugin/plugin.json in each skill folder under ~/.claude/skills and <project>/.claude/skills, honoring workspace trust and managed-settings blocking, and list its bundled agents, hooks and MCP servers.

kept.title: managedMcpServers managed setting as MCP source
kept.changed: A managedMcpServers managed setting supplies MCP servers that outrank all other scopes and override duplicates.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show organization-provided MCP servers, and may show user, project or local servers that are overridden by the managed definition.
kept.why: No row covers managed settings as a source of MCP servers or the managedMcpServers key.
kept.fix: Kitden would need to read the managedMcpServers key from the managed settings file and apply its precedence over other scopes.

kept.title: --setting-sources can exclude project rules
kept.changed: The --setting-sources flag decides whether project rules load; excluding project skips them.
kept.user_gets: Kitden lists project rules as loaded when a session started with --setting-sources excluding project does not load them.
kept.why: No row covers a flag that decides which instruction files load; CC-21 only lists where the files are.
kept.fix: Read how Claude Code is launched for the --setting-sources value to know whether project rules are loaded.

kept.title: Claude.ai-hosted marketplaces file
kept.changed: Marketplaces hosted on claude.ai are recorded in known_marketplaces_claudeai.json rather than known_marketplaces.json.
kept.user_gets: Marketplaces hosted on claude.ai are not listed.
kept.why: CC-14 names only known_marketplaces.json, and no row covers this second file.
kept.fix: Read known_marketplaces_claudeai.json in the plugins root as well as known_marketplaces.json.

kept.piece: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#Flags that load a plugin for one session
kept.title: CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS variable and disableSideloadFlags setting
kept.changed: Plugins can be loaded from folders named in the CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS variable, and a managed setting disableSideloadFlags can reject them.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show plugins loaded from folders in CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS, nor that disableSideloadFlags stops them loading.
kept.why: No row covers plugin folders set by an environment variable or the disableSideloadFlags setting.
kept.fix: Read the CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS environment variable and the managed disableSideloadFlags setting.

kept.piece: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading#Enabled in an `--add-dir` directory but not loaded
kept.title: --add-dir directories as a source of enabled plugins
kept.changed: Plugins enabled in settings files of directories added with --add-dir load only when trusted and when the session's --setting-sources include the file's source.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show plugins enabled by an added directory's settings, nor that --setting-sources stops some from loading.
kept.why: No row covers --add-dir directories or the --setting-sources setting that decides which settings files load.
kept.fix: Read the session's --add-dir directories and --setting-sources, then each added directory's .claude settings files and trust state.

kept.title: Hooks in skill and subagent frontmatter
kept.changed: Hooks can be defined in skill and subagent frontmatter.
kept.user_gets: Hooks defined in SKILL.md or agent file frontmatter are not shown.
kept.why: No row covers hooks in frontmatter of skills or agents.
kept.fix: Parse the hooks frontmatter of SKILL.md and agent files.

kept.title: Auto memory files MEMORY.md in project memory folder
kept.changed: Auto memory loads the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md from ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ at session start.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show the auto memory MEMORY.md that loads into each session as instructions.
kept.why: No row covers the auto memory folder; instruction file rows name CLAUDE.md, rules, commands and agents only.
kept.fix: Read MEMORY.md in ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ and show it as an instruction file with its load limit.

kept.row: Settings folder is `CODEX_HOME`, default `~/.codex`; settings in `config.toml`
kept.title: Codex profile config files next to config.toml
kept.changed: Settings can also live in `$CODEX_HOME/profile-name.config.toml` profile files selected with `--profile`, in addition to `config.toml` in the Codex home.
kept.user_gets: Entries defined only in a profile file are not listed, but they apply only when the user launches Codex with --profile.
kept.why: scan() reads only config.toml under codex_home. The quote does not say what a profile file can contain or how it merges, so a concrete wrong value cannot be named. The default config.toml behavior is unchanged.
kept.fix: Check what keys a profile file can hold and how Codex merges them. If it can hold mcp_servers or plugins, decide whether to read profile files in src/kitden/clients/codex.py scan().

kept.row: Skills the Claude app gives Claude Code (`anthropic-skills:docx`) are at `local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/<org>/<id>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` in the app's folder, some copied to `~/.claude/skills/synced/<org>_<id>/`; the newest copy is read (2026-11-12, version 2.1.309)
kept.title: Claude Code documents a synced/ folder under the plugins root
kept.changed: Synced plugins live in a `synced/` folder under the plugins root (default ~/.claude/plugins/synced), not only ~/.claude/skills/synced.
kept.user_gets: If synced skills now sit only under the plugins root, Kitden may find no description for them. The skill list would then show a missing description and size instead of a wrong one.
kept.why: _app_description only looks in ~/.claude/skills/synced and the app folder. The quote lists a plugins-root synced folder, but it does not say that skills moved there or that the old path stopped being used, so any effect on Kitden is a guess.
kept.fix: Check whether Claude Code 2.1.309 and later put synced skills under ~/.claude/plugins/synced. If so, add that path to the glob in _app_description in src/kitden/views/context_view.py and update the row.

kept.row: Skills in `~/.claude/skills` and `<project>/.claude/skills`, each a folder with `SKILL.md`
kept.title: Claude Code skills live reload mentions --add-dir skill folders
kept.changed: Skills are also read from a `.claude/skills/` inside an `--add-dir` directory, a place beyond the user and project skill folders the row names.
kept.user_gets: Skills from a directory added with --add-dir may be missing from Kitden's skill list, but the note does not clearly say this is new behaviour, and Kitden has no way to know the session's flags.
kept.why: skill_items is only called for the user and project skill folders in ClaudeCodeAdapter.scan and _project_files. The quote describes live reload and mentions --add-dir only in passing, so it is not a plain statement of a new loading behaviour, and the flag is not something Kitden can read from files.

kept.row: `disable-model-invocation: true` in SKILL.md keeps the description out of context (2026-11-06)
kept.title: disable-model-invocation also blocks subagent preload and scheduled tasks
kept.changed: The doc says disable-model-invocation: true also prevents preloading into subagents and running from a session-scoped scheduled task, and accepts yes/no/on/off/1/0 in any case as booleans. The row only states it keeps the description out of context.
kept.user_gets: The skill list state stays right for 'true'; the extra subagent and scheduled-task blocking is not shown.
kept.why: The quoted line only adds that the skill is also blocked from subagent preload and scheduled tasks. This does not change the auto-loading meaning that waits_to_be_asked() relies on. The boolean-variant claim is not in the quote, so Kitden's wrong output cannot be named.

kept.row: These commands work with no account: `claude --version`, `claude mcp add-json`, `get`, `list` and `remove`, `claude plugin validate --strict`, `marketplace add` and `remove`, `install`, `list --json`, `disable`, `enable` and `uninstall`; seen on Linux (2026-11-15, version 2.1.325). The nightly installs it with its own installer, `https://claude.ai/install.sh` run by `bash`, which puts `claude` in `~/.local/bin` and writes `~/.claude.json` with no account (2026-11-15, version 2.1.325, Linux)
kept.title: Claude Code plugin install refused without a TTY for command-source plugins
kept.changed: For plugins with command-source or headersHelper entries, install without a TTY is refused with exit 1 unless -y or --accept-command is given, so the no-account install command may behave differently.
kept.user_gets: Kitden's install step for such a plugin may fail with an error in a non-TTY run, and the row's claim that install works with no account is no longer fully true; nothing wrong is shown.
kept.why: plugin_install_step deliberately omits -y so a plugin that installs by running a command stops; the new refusal matches that intent, so Kitden stays right, but the row's blanket claim and the code comment about how it stops are now less precise.
kept.fix: In the contract-test row, note that install of plugins with command-source or headersHelper entries is refused without a TTY unless -y or --accept-command is given; optionally update the comment in `plugin_install_step` in `src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py`.

kept.row: `claude plugin uninstall <id> -s <scope> --keep-data --json`; it fails while settings still switch the plugin on
kept.title: Plugin uninstall reports settings_still_on when settings still enable the plugin
kept.changed: The uninstall command has new flags (--prune, -y, aliases remove/rm) and reports a settings_still_on failure code with --json; the failure while settings still switch the plugin on is confirmed and detailed (v2.1.282+). --json can't be combined with --prune.
kept.user_gets: Kitden's removal command still works as before, but the code comment that the command fails when settings still switch the plugin on no longer describes the failure code or the version (v2.1.282+).
kept.why: plugin_remove_step uses the same flags (-s, --keep-data, --json) and the same settings key as before, so the command still works. Only the comment about the failure behaviour is now less precise (it omits the failureCode settings_still_on and the v2.1.282 requirement).
kept.fix: Update the comment above plugin_remove_step in src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py to mention the settings_still_on failure code and that the settings check needs Claude Code v2.1.282 or later.

kept.row: `claude mcp add-json -s user <name> '<json>'` takes the entry as an argument, no stdin or file
kept.title: claude mcp add-json can read JSON from stdin
kept.changed: `claude mcp add-json` can now take the JSON from stdin with `-`, so the row's statement of argument only, no stdin, no longer holds.
kept.user_gets: Kitden keeps working and still writes secret-holding entries directly to ~/.claude.json, but the comment in _add_entry and the row saying add-json has no stdin option are no longer true.
kept.why: _add_entry still writes the same command and file edits, which the client accepts, so nothing breaks. Only the code comment and the row claiming no stdin or file option are now stale.
kept.fix: Update the comment in `_add_entry` in `src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py` and the research row to say add-json can read stdin with `-`. Optionally pass secret entries through stdin instead of editing the file, with a fallback inside a Claude Code session.

kept.row: These commands work with no account: `claude --version`, `claude mcp add-json`, `get`, `list` and `remove`, `claude plugin validate --strict`, `marketplace add` and `remove`, `install`, `list --json`, `disable`, `enable` and `uninstall`; seen on Linux (2026-11-15, version 2.1.325). The nightly installs it with its own installer, `https://claude.ai/install.sh` run by `bash`, which puts `claude` in `~/.local/bin` and writes `~/.claude.json` with no account (2026-11-15, version 2.1.325, Linux)
kept.title: Claude Code mcp add-json gains a stdin form
kept.changed: The `claude mcp add-json` command gains a stdin form; the account-free command list may need to cover it.
kept.user_gets: Kitden still works, but the comment in `_add_entry` saying add-json has no stdin option is no longer true on new versions, and secret entries are still written directly to the file.
kept.why: `_add_entry` still passes the existing add-json argument form, which works, and writes secret entries to `~/.claude.json` itself. The comment saying the docs show no stdin option is now stale, and the row's command list does not cover the stdin form.
kept.fix: Update the comment in `_add_entry` in `src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py`, and add the stdin form to the row. Optionally pass secret entries through `add-json <name> -` on stdin on versions that support it, instead of writing the file.

kept.title: claude mcp remove also deletes stored OAuth tokens for remote servers
kept.changed: claude mcp remove for a remote server now also deletes the stored OAuth tokens and client registration, beyond removing the entry.
kept.user_gets: Kitden removes the server entry as before, but the user is not told that stored OAuth tokens and client registration go too, so the remove cannot be undone by re-adding the entry alone.
kept.why: remove_step still runs the same command and edits the same key, so the action works and nothing shown is wrong. The row's description of what remove does is incomplete, and the Undo behaviour may not restore the sign-in.
kept.fix: In src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py, add a note to remove_step for remote servers saying that OAuth tokens and client registration are deleted too, and that the user should run `claude mcp logout <name>` first to revoke them.

kept.title: --settings flag can enable plugins
kept.changed: A settings value passed at launch with --settings can carry enabledPlugins and overrides user, project and local.
kept.user_gets: Kitden does not show plugins enabled or disabled by a --settings value for a session.
kept.why: No row covers the --settings launch flag as a source of enabledPlugins.
kept.fix: Kitden would need to read the --settings value from the running client's launch command.

kept.title: Skills from --add-dir directories
kept.changed: A directory passed with `--add-dir` can supply skills from its `.claude/skills` folder for that session.
kept.user_gets: Skills loaded from additional directories are not shown.
kept.why: The directory is passed on the command line in a session, and no row covers it as a skill source.
kept.fix: Read the `--add-dir` directories of a session and their `.claude/skills` folders.

kept.title: Plugin manifest optionalDependencies install extra plugins
kept.changed: Plugin manifests can list optional dependency plugins that are installed along with the plugin and can be disabled or uninstalled separately.
kept.user_gets: Plugins pulled in as optional dependencies may load without Kitden showing where they came from or linking them to the parent plugin.
kept.why: No row covers plugin manifest contents or dependency-installed plugins; rows cover installed_plugins.json and enabledPlugins only.
kept.fix: Read the plugin manifest's optionalDependencies and the resulting installed plugin entries to show dependency plugins.

kept.row: Instruction files: `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` at the project root, `rules/*.md`, `commands/*.md`, `agents/*.md` in `.claude`, sub-folders too (2026-10-22)
kept.title: Claude Code skips CLAUDE.md files over 4 MiB
kept.changed: CLAUDE.md instruction files over 4 MiB are skipped entirely; subdirectory CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rules have a smaller per-file limit.
kept.user_gets: The user sees an oversized CLAUDE.md listed as loaded and believes its instructions apply, when Claude Code ignores the file.
kept.why: _instruction_files returns every CLAUDE.md path and instruction_items shows it, and nothing in claude_code.py checks size. The size check may live in instruction_items in base.py, which was not provided, so this is a guess.
kept.fix: In src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py (or instruction_items in base.py), mark a CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md file over 4 MiB as not loaded, or show its state as unknown, instead of listing it as loaded.

kept.title: syncClaudeAiPlugins setting decides whether synced plugins load
kept.changed: A user or managed setting `syncClaudeAiPlugins` set to false stops downloading claude.ai plugins and stops loading already synced ones.
kept.user_gets: Kitden may show synced plugins that the setting stops from loading, with no sign of the switch.
kept.why: No row names syncClaudeAiPlugins; CC-15 only says @⁠synced ids have no install to remove.
kept.fix: Read `syncClaudeAiPlugins` from user and managed settings and hide or mark synced plugins when it is false.

kept.title: Claude Code can disable synced plugins from the CLI and /plugin tab
kept.changed: `claude plugin disable <name>@⁠synced` saves `"<name>@⁠synced": false` in user-level enabledPlugins; and it refuses a plugin the organization requires.
kept.user_gets: The hint on @⁠synced plugins says to change them in the Claude app, although they can now be disabled locally.
kept.why: scan() gives @⁠synced plugins ACCOUNT scope with ACCOUNT_HINT and no toggle action, a stale statement now that the CLI disables them. Kitden still reads enabledPlugins correctly, so values shown stay right.
kept.fix: Update ACCOUNT_HINT or the @⁠synced handling in src/kitden/clients/claude_code.py to say they can be disabled with `claude plugin disable <name>@⁠synced`, or offer a toggle for them.

kept.title: syncClaudeAiSkills setting decides whether synced skills load
kept.changed: Setting syncClaudeAiSkills to false stops downloading synced skills, and at next start moves existing ones to ~/.claude/skills/.trash/ so they no longer load.
kept.user_gets: Kitden may show synced skills that the setting has turned off, and does not show that the key or the .trash folder removes them.
kept.why: No row names the syncClaudeAiSkills key or the ~/.claude/skills/.trash/ folder; CC-32 only covers where synced skills are read from.
kept.fix: Read syncClaudeAiSkills in the settings files and skip skills under ~/.claude/skills/.trash/.
